PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: artifact-davids-harp-symbol-of-music-and-hope-close-up
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Prop/artifact guard: transfer only material response, patina, highlight rolloff, and photographic presentation. Do not add a glowing sword, sacred symbols, blood, or human hands unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
DAVID'S HARP - SYMBOL OF MUSIC AND HOPE — CLOSE-UP: HERO PROP DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, SCALE, AND CONTINUITY.

Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Hero prop close-up of King David's ancient biblical harp from the Harrowing of Hell liberation sequence, the instrument that has remained at his side through centuries of captivity with its strings broken and silent. This is a portable Near Eastern / ancient Levantine lyre-harp hybrid of the kind associated with the shepherd-king and psalmist: a curved wooden yoke frame roughly the size of a seated musician's lap instrument, not a modern concert harp. The resonating body is carved from dense, dark-aged hardwood—olive, cedar, or acacia character—deep walnut to near-black brown with warm honey undertones where divine amber light rakes across raised grain. Centuries of handling have polished the grip zones to a soft sheen while the rest of the surface is dry, micro-cracked, and dusted with fine pale ash and stone grit from Hell's chamber floor. The soundboard shows hairline checks following the wood grain; a few small chips and worn edges speak of long travel and rough imprisonment, never modern damage or machine tooling.

The curved arms and cross-yoke are joined with ancient mortise craftsmanship, seams darkened by age and soot. Intricate low-relief carvings wind across the body and arms: stylized vine scrolls, olive leaves, small rosettes, and abstract psalm-like ornamental bands suggesting divine praise without any readable modern lettering, calligraphy blocks, or legible text of any kind. The carvings catch soft raking light so ridges read as tactile wood, not painted decoration. Where gilding once existed, only ghost traces of worn gold leaf cling in recessed grooves—faint royal memory matching David's faded blue-and-gold garments—never bright new foil.

Multiple gut or sinew strings span the instrument; most are snapped mid-length, frayed, and curled loosely, their broken ends hanging limp as visual proof of centuries of silence. A few remaining strands sag slack and untuned, pale amber-tan against the dark wood. Small wooden or bone tuning pegs sit along the yoke, some slightly askew, surfaces polished by fingers long ago. Scale reads as a true hand-held ancient harp/lyre: complete object fully visible in frame from resonating base through yoke and string field, hero-prop product framing for production continuity, not a partial crop that hides the form.

Optional restrained human presence only as supporting scale if needed: a portion of a dignified middle-aged freed king's hand—weathered Mediterranean skin, no jewelry—may cradle the lower body or rest lightly against the frame at the edge of frame, fingers gentle and reverent, implying David has just been freed and still carries the harp. Do not feature a full face or competing portrait; the harp is the sole hero subject. Environment context is the inner chamber of Hell at the moment of liberation transforming toward hope: soft warm amber and pale gold divine radiance (approximately 4500–6500K god-light quality) rakes across the wood as key light from upper camera-left, revealing grain, dust motes in a thin volumetric shaft, and faint specular glints on remaining gold flecks. Subtle cooler residual fill from distant blue torch influence may kiss the shadow side so the object still feels grounded in the fortress before full marble transformation, without overpowering the warm hope palette. Background is shallow-depth soft bokeh of dark stone and dust, never sharp architecture competing with the prop.

Camera language: extreme cinematic prop close-up, roughly 85–100mm equivalent portrait telephoto feel, slight three-quarter angle that shows both the carved face of the body and the depth of the broken string field, shallow depth of field with crisp focus on the carved wood and severed string ends, gentle falloff toward the rear arm. Aspect framing suitable for 2.39:1 extraction with the complete instrument centered and readable. Color grade: warm amber, honey wood, muted gold remnants, desaturated ash dust, deep brown shadows—sacred biblical epic tone, photoreal live-action production still, physically coherent materials, subsurface wood warmth, fine particulate atmosphere. No modern strings, piano pins, metal machine heads, plastic, chrome, factory lacquer, logo brands, barcodes, museum plaques, or contemporary harp hardware. No readable text, no captions, no watermarks, no borders, no UI. Continuity lock: this is the same broken-string ancient wooden harp that remains at David's side when the righteous are freed; strings stay broken (silence of ages); wood is aged and ash-dusted; carvings suggest psalms and praise without legible writing; warm amber liberation light marks restored hope and the return of music as symbol, not a newly repaired instrument. Neutral production reference framing, the complete object visible, accurate materials and scale, no labels or text.
